I couldn't find an Alberta poverty rate for people with disabilities, so I'm not giving one. The only Statistics Canada table I found on poverty by disability status is Canada-only (the cube lists "Canada" as its sole geography). It has no provincial breakdown, and I didn't find a separate provincial table.

**Canada-wide figure (not Alberta):**
- About 12.6% of persons aged 15+ with disabilities were in poverty in 2024. This uses the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), which is Canada's official poverty line. The 2023 figure was 12.8%.
- Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0090-01, vector v1793292452, reference year 2024 (released 2026-04-29). Canadian Income Survey; the estimate excludes the territories.
- Data-quality code is 4. I didn't check what that means for this table, so treat the estimate with that in mind.

For Alberta, the next place to look would be a custom tabulation from Statistics Canada's Canadian Income Survey or Canadian Survey on Disability. Provincial estimates for this group may also be too unreliable to publish.

I couldn't find an Alberta poverty rate for people with disabilities. The only official source I found is Canada-wide.

Statistics Canada table 11-10-0090-01 (Canadian Income Survey, poverty by disability status) is published for Canada only, and the national estimate excludes the territories. It has no provincial breakdown. I also searched the federal and Alberta open-data portals and found no Alberta table. I haven't estimated one.

**Canada, persons aged 15+ with disabilities, Market Basket Measure (MBM, 2023 base), reference year 2024:**
- With disabilities: 12.6% (v1793292452)
- Without disabilities: 8.4% (v1793292497)
- The 2023 values were 12.8% and 8.3%.
- On the older 2018-base MBM, the 2023 rate was 12.1% for people with disabilities (v1412450234) versus 7.8% for people without (v1412450354). There is no 2024 value on that base.
- Statistics Canada flags these estimates with quality indicator code 4. I didn't check what that code means.

Alberta's rate may differ from the national figure, so please don't treat 12.6% as Alberta's. A provincial figure may be available as a custom tabulation from Statistics Canada, or from the 2022 Canadian Survey on Disability, but I didn't find it.

Source: Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0090-01, https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1110009001. Released 2026-04-29.

I couldn't find an Alberta-specific poverty rate for people with disabilities. The table I found, Statistics Canada 11‑10‑0090‑01 (Poverty and low-income statistics by disability status), is published for Canada only, with no provincial breakdown. I didn't find another provincial source, so I won't estimate an Alberta figure.

**National figures (2024, Market Basket Measure, 2023 base, persons aged 15+; excludes the territories):**
- Persons with disabilities: **12.6%** (v1793292452)
- Persons without disabilities: 8.4% (v1793292497)

The 2023 rate for persons with disabilities was 12.8%.

The Canadian Survey on Disability (2022) may have provincial poverty or low-income breakdowns. I didn't find a dataset with them in this search. A custom tabulation from Statistics Canada might also work.

Source: Statistics Canada, table 11‑10‑0090‑01, https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/5ac0dd76-f4ce-46b9-a3bf-9c35925156d6
